_doc: Demo mock-response fixtures keyed by eval id. Used to prove the runner pipeline end-to-end without burning Anthropic tokens. with-skill responses are crafted to satisfy the eval expectations; baseline responses simulate a model relying on training memory (gets the broad strokes but misses the modern resource names + cards).

A1-cloudflare-dns-record.baseline:
```hcl
resource "cloudflare_record" "api" {
  zone_id = "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353"
  name    = "api"
  value   = "203.0.113.42"
  type    = "A"
  proxied = true
  ttl     = 1
}
```
A1-cloudflare-dns-record.with-skill:
Per knowledge card cloudflare-resource-renames-v5, use cloudflare_dns_record (provider v5+):
```hcl
resource "cloudflare_dns_record" "api" {
  zone_id = "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353"
  name    = "api"
  type    = "A"
  content = "203.0.113.42"
  ttl     = 1
  proxied = true
}
```

A3-import-cloudflare-dns-record.baseline:
```hcl
resource "cloudflare_record" "foo" {
  zone_id = "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353"
  name    = "foo"
  type    = "A"
  value   = ""
}
```

Import:
```
terraform import cloudflare_record.foo 372e67954025e0ba6aaa6d586b9e0b59
```
A3-import-cloudflare-dns-record.with-skill:
Per knowledge card cloudflare-resource-renames-v5 — use cloudflare_dns_record:
```hcl
resource "cloudflare_dns_record" "foo" {
  zone_id = "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353"
  name    = "foo"
  type    = "A"
  content = "203.0.113.42"
}
```

Import using composite ID `<zone_id>/<record_id>`:
```
terraform import cloudflare_dns_record.foo 023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/372e67954025e0ba6aaa6d586b9e0b59
```

A12-cloudflare-record-deprecated.baseline: Yes, cloudflare_record is the standard resource for DNS records. You can keep using it.
A12-cloudflare-record-deprecated.with-skill:
No — per knowledge card cloudflare-resource-renames-v5, the legacy cloudflare_record was renamed to cloudflare_dns_record in CF provider v5 (Sep 2024). Migrate with `terraform state mv` and update your config to use cloudflare_dns_record.
```hcl
resource "cloudflare_dns_record" "example" {
  zone_id = var.zone_id
  name    = "example"
  type    = "A"
  content = "203.0.113.10"
}
```

A12-do-i-need-dynamodb-for-locks.baseline: Yes — for the S3 backend you need a DynamoDB table for state locking. Add a `dynamodb_table` arg pointing to your lock table.
